## Goal

Fully investigate the root cause proposal that the llama-proxy reported **busy** for the entire 7h09m overnight idle window (2026-08-07/08, 03:18–10:26Z local) on 192.168.0.199:8000, blocking **all** herdr downtime dispatch across 5+ worklogs, and — if confirmed — design and implement a fix.

## Origin

Proposal from RCA WL-0MSK9TUCA00206M7 (ContextHub worklog, completed 2026-08-09, audit-passed). That RCA's H6 hypothesis concluded the proxy's `GET /llama/local/status` reported busy throughout the window, so every herdr downtime worker evaluated NOT-idle and never passed the 4-minute continuous-idle dispatch gate. The RCA could not verify the idle-window status payloads directly (see evidence gap below) and explicitly delegated the proxy-side investigation here.

## Evidence from the RCA (ContextHub worklog)

### Observations

1. **Continuous polling, zero dispatch attempts:** ~8 pollers (this host's 5 herdr worklist panes + pi/opencode statuslines) polled `GET /llama/local/status` at ~15.9 polls/min for 7h09m. Zero dispatch attempts in the window — no `dispatch_cleanup`, no `local_dispatch_denied`, no `lease_renewed` events; zero error records in any downtime dispatch log (no three-strike pauses; a no-candidate cooldown would have stopped polling, and it did not).
2. **Proxy health:** `proxy.log.2026-08-08_05` contains only `status_request` (5722) and `lease_released` (51); llama-server up with Qwen3 loaded; zero local model requests 04:18–11:26 local.

### Candidate mechanisms (root-cause proposal)

- **H6a — stuck global `active_queries` counter (smoking gun):** the status endpoint's `active_query` reads the GLOBAL counter (`srv.active_queries > 0`). Two abandoned local streams (sessions `019fdea8` @ 23:58Z, `019fdebf` @ 00:23Z — started but never logged "Stream finished") would leave the global counter incremented forever. At the time of the RCA the proxy had recovery only for the LOCAL counter (`_recover_stuck_local_active_queries`), not the global one. A post-restart status of `active_query=true` with 3/3 slots free, no lease, and no local requests in flight was observed — consistent with a stuck counter.
- **H6b — lingering local dispatch lease:** the last audit-wave pane (session `019fdf5f`) held a local dispatch lease until **03:19:53Z** (idle-timeout release right at the idle-window start) → `local_lease_active=true` → busy for the window's first ~90 min.
- **H6c — `/slots` failure during model reload:** llama-server.5.log shows a fresh spawn + model reload at the window start; during reload `/slots` returns 500 → `available_slots=0` → workers correctly see busy. Any silent `/slots` failures would extend this.

### Evidence gap

- The idle-window `status_request` log lines were **bare (no fields)** — the observability fix (client IP + full status payload, LP-0MSK9XXCN0077CMA / LP-0MSKV3IEQ004ZV88) only landed 2026-08-08T15:59:30 local, AFTER the window. So "the status reported busy" is a reconstruction from the two abandoned streams + lingering lease, not a direct measurement. **The investigation must either reconstruct the idle-window status from surviving artifacts (sessions, leases, llama-server logs) or explicitly confirm/refute each mechanism with direct evidence.**

## Related existing work (do not duplicate)

- **LP-0MSL1OX51003DOP4** (completed, in_review): periodic in-process recovery for the stuck global `active_queries` counter — verify this covers H6a's failure mode end-to-end; close gaps if not.
- **LP-0MSK9XXCN0077CMA** / **LP-0MSKV3IEQ004ZV88** (completed, in_review): status_request client IP + full response payload logging — the observability prerequisite; verify deployment.
- **LP-0MSL2ZLLS009RVKR** (open, idea): expose `local_active_query` in the status payload so remote streams don't mask local idleness — related but distinct.
- Lease lifecycle fixes (release-on-finish, orphan cleanup, counter-decrement hardening) largely exist as completed items — the investigation should confirm the specific window's lease path (session `019fdf5f`) is covered.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Mechanism confirmed or refuted with evidence:** for each candidate (H6a stuck global counter, H6b lingering lease, H6c `/slots` failure during reload), the investigation determines from surviving logs/artifacts whether it was active during 2026-08-07T21:55Z–2026-08-08T10:26Z, with specific log/session/lease evidence.
- [ ] **Fix designed for every confirmed mechanism:** where LP-0MSL1OX51003DOP4 or the lease-lifecycle items already cover a confirmed mechanism, state the coverage explicitly (with a verification result); where a mechanism is confirmed and uncovered, design the fix.
- [ ] **Automated tests reproduce the stuck state** and assert recovery/status correctness (unit tests mirroring the RCA scenario: abandoned stream → counter never decremented; lease held past stream end).
- [ ] **Idle-window status is answered, not assumed:** the investigation concludes — from evidence, or explicitly as unverifiable — whether `GET /llama/local/status` actually reported idle-capable (active_query=false, slots free) at any ≥4-min stretch during the window.
- [ ] **Dispatch resume verified:** after fix deployment, a herdr downtime dispatch is observed in a worklog's `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` on the next ≥4-min idle window (end-to-end closure).
data.title: RCA: llama-proxy reported busy for entire 7h09m idle window (2026-08-07/08) — zero herdr downtime dispatch; investigate and design fix

# Feature: Proxy-side proactive session compaction (Tier 1)

**STATUS: DEFERRED — implementation delayed until client-side compaction
results are available.** Client-side compaction machinery is now in place in
ContextHub (Compact-and-Continue WL-0MR269PDV00970YP, auto-continue
WL-0MSMGGPWR000MZ0O; gate-response wiring WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6). Per
operator decision (2026-08-28), server-side compaction must not be
implemented until results from the client-side effort are reviewed; this
item is parked (status `blocked`) pending that review.

Implementation of the F4 recommendation (LP-0MTC8BWV50012WSW,
`docs/session-compaction-recommendations.md`) within the two-tier scheme of
LP-0MTCW79RR000LFMJ. The proxy compacts the session at **prompt-assembly
time** when estimated tokens exceed the trigger — no round trip, no
client-side coordination.

## Behavior (both modes — Strategy C, summarize-first)

Per operator decision (2026-08-28), serve-side compaction uses the hybrid
Strategy C in **both** fast and cheap modes, with the **first prompt always
retained verbatim**.

### Retention invariant (fast AND cheap)

The compacted prompt MUST always contain, unchanged:

1. the system prompt;
2. the **very first user prompt** (the original task statement/setup, which
   carries essential instructions);
3. the most recent turns within budget.

Everything between the first prompt and the recent window is folded into a
summary injected at the top of the prompt (below the retained first prompt).

### Fast mode — Strategy C

- **Trigger:** `estimated_tokens > 58,300` (= 0.70 × per-slot clamp 83,285).
  Fires before the existing `context_pressure_warn_ratio` (0.8 × 83,285 =
  66.6K) so compaction is proactive, not reactive.
- **Target:** compacted prompt ≤ 38,000 tokens (`local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold`,
  fast profile): retain system prompt + first prompt + recent turns; fold
  the rest into a summary.
- **Backstop:** only if the session still exceeds budget after summarizing,
  drop oldest non-first turns (whole turns, never splittable, never the
  system prompt or first prompt), logged.
- **Automatic** on breach.

### Cheap mode — Strategy C (hybrid)

- **Trigger:** `estimated_tokens > 43,000` (= 0.70 × static clamp 61,440).
- **Target:** compacted prompt ≤ 30,000 tokens: same retention invariant +
  summary of the middle.
- **Non-compactable** (summarizer unavailable, or still over budget after
  compaction): route remote with guidance — never silent remote fallback,
  never near-full-slot local prefill (LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D AC4).
- **Automatic** on breach.

## Implementation approach

- **Trigger hook:** reuse the existing `context_pressure` machinery in
  `proxy/provider.py` (`context_pressure_ratio` / `should_warn_context_pressure`,
  LP-0MSDCLQ2W001LGWC). Add a configurable compaction trigger ratio
  (default 0.70), distinct from the 0.8 diagnostic warn ratio (unchanged).
- **Compaction at prompt assembly:** session history is a message list;
  summarization/truncation operates on it before dispatch. Composes with
  slot save/restore (compacted prompts restore cleanly under the
  persistence cap).
- **Summarizer:** short proxy-generated summary (cheap local call) injected
  at the top of the prompt; with summarizer-unavailable fallback to the
  truncate backstop.
- **Logging:** every compaction event logs session, before/after estimated
  tokens, turns summarized, turns dropped, summary length — traceability
  for quality regressions (F3 §7). Nothing is silent.
- **Rollout phases:**
  1. **Warn-only dry-run** — advisory (would-summarize/would-drop) log +
     stats for 48h; validate churn (< 1 compaction/session/hour) against
     F1/F2 distributions; **no dispatch behavior change**.
  2. **Enforcement** — gated on the quality experiment (LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ)
     passing its bar AND operator review of client-side compaction results.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 Both modes: compacted prompt retains system prompt + very first user
  prompt verbatim + recent turns; middleware summarized (never silently
  dropped).
- AC2 Fast: est > 58,300 → compacted to ≤ 38K; backstop drop only for
  non-summarizable middle turns, logged, never system/first prompt.
- AC3 Cheap: est > 43,000 → compacted to ≤ 30K; non-compactable → remote
  with guidance (never silent remote, never near-full-slot local dispatch).
- AC4 Trigger routed through `context_pressure` machinery; compaction
  trigger ratio 0.70 configurable; 0.8 warn ratio behavior unchanged.
- AC5 All compaction events logged (session, before/after est tokens, turns
  summarized, turns dropped, summary length).
- AC6 Warn-only dry-run phase produces advisory logs + churn stats with
  zero dispatch changes; dry-run threshold validation recorded.
- AC7 Unit tests: retention invariant (first prompt kept), summary path,
  truncate backstop boundaries, turn-split prohibition, non-compactable
  routing, warn-only mode. Full suite green.
- AC8 Enforcement only after experiment (LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ) passes its
  bar AND client-side compaction review (ContextHub WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6) is
  complete; no behavior change in warn-only phase.

## Interaction analysis (from F4 §5)

- **Slot save/restore:** summary + recent turns are byte-stable → clean
  restores under the persistence cap.
- **Hard-routing-cap companion (Tier 2, LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S):** cap at
  70K/61.4K is the final bypass guard; compaction trigger fires below it so
  sessions rarely reach the cap.
- **KV-cache quantization (LP-0MSDCLQ2W001LGWC):** additive — compaction
  shrinks context length, q8_0 shrinks bytes/token; both raise decode
  headroom.

## Out of scope

- Client-side compaction UX (ContextHub owns it; see WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6).
- 150K–480K HTTP-400 cluster (LP-0MSC1BNP90017L9K).
- Changing the 0.8 diagnostic warn ratio.

## Dependencies

- Depends on LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ (quality experiment) for the enforcement
  go/no-go.
- **Blocked pending:** client-side compaction results (ContextHub
  WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6 and completed compact-and-continue machinery) —
  operator decision 2026-08-28 to delay server-side until those are
  reviewed.
- Complementary to LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S (Tier 2 hard cap + cheap gate).
data.title: Implement proxy-side proactive session compaction (Tier 1: truncate 58.3K / hybrid 43K)

# Intake Brief: When a request cannot be processed because there are no available models include a retry timer (LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI)

> **DRAFT — awaiting producer answers to the OPEN QUESTIONs in the Appendix.**
> The scope below is the agent's proposed reading of the seed intent; the
> alternatives are listed in Q1/Q2 of the Appendix.

## Headline

When the proxy rejects a request because no model/provider/slot can serve it,
the error response must carry a machine-readable retry instruction
(`Retry-After` header **and** a matching `retry_after` JSON field) so a client
can automatically re-issue the request when capacity returns, instead of
surfacing an opaque error. The generic and time-window exhaustion 503 paths
already do this; this item closes the remaining "no models available" paths
that do not, and defines the shared contract they must all satisfy.

## Problem statement

Clients reach an upstream LLM through this proxy. When every model that can
serve a request is unavailable — all providers in the fallback chain are in
cooldown, outside their `available_times` window, or usage-limit quarantined,
or all local slots are busy — the proxy rejects the request. For an unattended
agent (herdr worker / Pi session) to recover automatically, the rejection must
tell it *how long* to wait. The generic and time-window exhaustion 503 paths
already emit a truthful `Retry-After` header and `retry_after` body field
(LP-0MT654ISW002QVH4, LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G), but some capacity rejections still
omit any retry instruction, so a client cannot distinguish "retry in N
seconds" from a terminal error.

The most clearly documented gap is the **local slot-exhaustion 429**:
`proxy/README.md` states it returns the JSON body *"(no `Retry-After`
header)"*. The **router concurrency-limit 503** (`Server overloaded: N
queries active. Retry later.`) also returns no `Retry-After`/`retry_after`.

## Users

- **Local agent (herdr worker / Pi session)** — the primary beneficiary.
  Receives a capacity rejection and needs a concrete retry instruction so its
  recovery classifier can wait and retry, rather than surfacing
  `Unrecognized error:` or hammering the proxy.
- **Proxy operator / on-call engineer** — needs every capacity rejection to be
  self-describing (which capacity was missing, and when to come back) so the
  response alone explains an overnight failure.

### Example user stories

- As an agent whose request hits local slot exhaustion, I want the 429 to tell
  me how many seconds to wait, so I retry automatically when a slot frees up.
- As an agent whose request is rejected because the server is overloaded, I
  want the 503 to carry a retry timer, so my recovery loop backs off instead of
  retrying immediately.
- As an operator, I want every "no models available" rejection to use the same
  `Retry-After` + `retry_after` contract, so I can reason about (and document)
  a single behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

Proposed scope (see Q1/Q2): bring the remaining proxy capacity rejections up to
the existing retry-hint contract.

- **AC1 — Shared contract:** Every response that rejects a request because no
  model/provider/slot can serve it includes both a `Retry-After` HTTP header
  (integer delta-seconds) and a `retry_after` JSON body field, with the **same**
  non-negative integer value.
- **AC2 — Local slot exhaustion (429):** `_build_exhausted_response(all_local_slot_exhaustion=True)`
  includes `Retry-After` + `retry_after`, derived from real capacity (at minimum
  `server.slot_unavailable_retry_after`), consistent with the existing
  `_build_slot_exhaustion_response` 503. Verified by a unit/integration test
  asserting status `429`, `code == "all_slots_exhausted"`, and the header/body
  retry value.
- **AC3 — Router concurrency limit (503):** The concurrency-limit rejection
  (currently `HTTPException(503, detail="Server overloaded: N queries active.
  Retry later.")`) includes `Retry-After` + `retry_after`. Verified by a test
  asserting status `503` and the retry hint.
- **AC4 — Truthful, not hardcoded:** `retry_after` is `0` only when capacity is
  genuinely available; otherwise positive. For slot exhaustion it is bounded by
  the configured slot retry value; for concurrency it reflects a documented
  bound. Verified by tests.
- **AC5 — Additive-only contract:** The existing human-readable `error` prose
  and stable `code` values (`all_exhausted`, `outside_time_window`,
  `all_slots_exhausted`) are unchanged; only the retry instruction is added.
  Verified by the existing exhaustion-contract tests still passing.
- **AC6 — Testing/validation:** At least one automated test per patched path
  asserts the status code, `Retry-After` header, `retry_after` body field and
  `code`.
- **AC7 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments, `proxy/README.md` (the slot-exhaustion
  contract currently documents "no `Retry-After` header"), and any relevant
  wiki or docs-site entries.
- **AC8 — Full suite:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Additive-only:** do not remove or reword existing `error` prose or `code`
  values — older clients key on them (epic constraint LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO).
- **Do not change availability policy:** `available_times` windows are
  intentional; do not wake a provider outside its window to satisfy a retry.
- **No proxy restart:** changes ship through the normal build → test → commit
  workflow; never kill the proxy as part of the fix.
- **Client-side classifier changes are out of scope in this repo** — the
  ContextHub recovery/retry modules live in the ContextHub repository (see Q3
  and Related work).

## Existing state

- Generic exhaustion 503 (`_build_exhausted_response`) and time-window 503
  (`_build_time_window_exhausted_response`) in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` already
  emit `Retry-After` + `retry_after`, computed by `_compute_retry_after` from
  real availability (cooldowns, window edges, usage-limit resets).
- 429 local slot exhaustion (`_build_exhausted_response(all_local_slot_exhaustion=True)`)
  emits `{"error": "All providers exhausted", "code": "all_slots_exhausted",
  "message": "Model server busy: 0/N slots available. Retry later."}` with **no**
  `Retry-After` header and **no** `retry_after` field. `proxy/README.md` documents
  this gap explicitly.
- The router concurrency-limit rejection (`proxy/proxy/router.py`, ~line 1055)
  returns a bare `HTTPException(503, "Server overloaded: N queries active.
  Retry later.")` with no retry hint.
- The sibling `_build_slot_exhaustion_response` (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`)
  is the reference implementation: it already sets `Retry-After` and
  `retry_after` from `server.slot_unavailable_retry_after`.
- Client side (ContextHub `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/`):
  `retry-logic.ts` parses `Retry-After` / `Retry-After-Ms` headers and the
  `retry_after` body field, but caps the applied delay at `maxDelayMs = 60000`
  (60 s). A multi-hour "come back online" wait is therefore not honoured as-is
  by the current client (see Q3).

## Desired change

1. Make the 429 local slot-exhaustion response carry `Retry-After` and
   `retry_after` (reuse `_get_slot_unavailable_retry_after`).
2. Make the router concurrency-limit 503 carry `Retry-After` and `retry_after`.
3. Audit the remaining "no models available" rejections (see Q2) and give each a
   consistent retry instruction, or explicitly record why it has none.
4. Update `proxy/README.md` and code comments to document the unified contract.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_build_exhausted_response` 429 branch (~line 2955),
  `_get_slot_unavailable_retry_after` (~line 2794), `_compute_retry_after` (~line 2257).
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — concurrency-limit rejection (~line 1055).
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_build_slot_exhaustion_response` (~line 570) as the
  reference implementation for the retry-hint contract.
- `proxy/tests/test_exhaustion_error_code.py`, `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_admission.py` — extend/add retry-hint assertions.
- `proxy/README.md` — exhaustion / capacity-response contract section (~line 690).

## Related work

| Item | Relationship |
|------|-------------|
| LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO — Epic: Overnight remote-chain exhaustion | Related epic; the generic/time-window 503 retry contract was delivered by its children. This item covers the *remaining* capacity paths. |
| LP-0MT654ISW002QVH4 — Honest Retry-After: emit real provider availability windows | Predecessor: introduced truthful `retry_after`/`Retry-After` on the exhaustion 503. |
| LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G — Exhaustion 503: stable machine-readable error code | Predecessor: added `code` discriminators. |
| LP-0MU56ZKQD005SX08 — Chain-hold: bound hold duration by the real `retry_after` | Predecessor: bounds the hold by the retry timer. |
| LP-0MQHCG7FA005U886 — Strengthen Retry-After test assertion | Prior test-quality work on `Retry-After`. |
| LP-0MQS6MPK9000UIZK — Phase 2: Queue overflow rejection with Retry-After | Precedent: queue-overflow rejection already carries `Retry-After`. |
| ContextHub `WL-0MU56ZSSB0054D8W` / `WL-0MT656GDS0052FTK` | Client-side recovery classifier/retry handling (separate repository) — decides how the retry timer is acted on, including the 60 s cap. |

## Risks & assumptions

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|
| Scope overlaps the completed overnight-exhaustion epic, duplicating delivered work | Q1 confirms whether this item covers only the *remaining* paths or is superseded. |
| A retry hint on the concurrency-limit 503 could cause a retry storm | Use a conservative, documented bound; clients also apply upward jitter. |
| Changing the 429 body could break the existing `all_slots_exhausted` contract tests | Additive-only: the header/field are added, existing fields retained. |
| The client 60 s cap means a multi-hour wait is not honoured even with a correct hint | Q3 decides whether to align the client cap (ContextHub item) or accept the cap. |
| Scope creep (adding retry semantics to unrelated 4xx, e.g. compaction gate / single-flight) | Q2 bounds the set of responses in scope; extras become linked work items. |

Assumptions (to be confirmed):

- The proxy is the correct repository for this item; client recovery changes
  live in ContextHub (epic constraint).
- `Retry-After` is expressed as integer delta-seconds, consistent with all
  existing proxy responses.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope / supersession):** This item (created 2026-09-16) predates the
  overnight-exhaustion epic LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO (created 2026-09-17), whose
  children already added `Retry-After` + `retry_after` + stable codes to the
  generic and time-window exhaustion 503. Which is intended?
  (a) Scope this item to the remaining proxy capacity rejections that lack a
  retry timer (429 local slot exhaustion, concurrency-limit 503) and audit the
  rest; (b) treat it as an end-to-end verification of the whole "no models
  available" retry contract on the proxy; (c) close it as superseded by the
  epic; (d) include the client-side ContextHub classifier in scope.
  **Recommended:** (a) — it is the only clearly undocumented gap and does not
  duplicate the epic.
  — **OPEN QUESTION** (no answer recorded; awaiting producer).
- **Q2 (which responses count as "no models available"):** Which rejections
  must carry a retry timer? (a) All fallback-chain exhaustion 503s, plus the
  429 local slot-exhaustion path, plus the router concurrency-limit 503;
  (b) only the "all providers exhausted" 503; (c) every 4xx/5xx that stops the
  request, including the compaction-gate 429 and the session single-flight 429.
  **Recommended:** (a) — these are the capacity-availability rejections; the
  compaction gate and single-flight are request-shape/duplicate-work signals,
  not missing capacity.
  — **OPEN QUESTION** (no answer recorded; awaiting producer).
- **Q3 (retry-horizon / client cap):** The ContextHub client caps an applied
  `Retry-After` at 60 s (`retry-logic.ts` `maxDelayMs = 60000`), so a truthful
  multi-hour overnight `retry_after` is not actually waited out by the client.
  Should this item (a) emit the true wait and raise the client cap via a linked
  ContextHub work item so the client sleeps until models return; or (b) emit a
  bounded wait (≤ 60 s) so the client retries periodically? **Recommended:**
  (a) — the seed intent is "retry when the models come back online", which a
  60 s cap cannot satisfy for multi-hour gaps; the client change is a linked
  ContextHub item.
  — **OPEN QUESTION** (no answer recorded; awaiting producer).
data.title: When a request cannot be processed because there are no available models include a retry timer

# Auto-derive large-context routing thresholds (physical clamp + latency-derived economic ceiling)

## Goal (user story)

As a proxy operator, I want the large-context **warm** routing threshold to auto-derive from the active model's context size and slot count — using a physical per-slot clamp plus a latency-derived economic ceiling — so that changing the slot count or the model context size never requires manual threshold recalculation, while never routing latency-destroying warm contexts local. The **cold** (new-token) threshold stays a fixed per-mode economic value.

## Problem statement

`local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold` is a single absolute value (100,000) shared by every mode profile and clamped at runtime to the physical per-slot capacity:

```
effective_warm = min(configured_warm, per_slot_cap)
per_slot_cap   = local_model_ctx_size // slots - 4096
```

The same configured value therefore has wildly different effective meaning per profile, and operators must manually recalculate it whenever the slot schedule or model context size changes:

| Profile | Slots | Per-slot cap | Configured warm | Effective warm | % of cap |
|---------|-------|--------------|-----------------|----------------|----------|
| fast    | 1     | 258,048      | 100,000         | 100,000        | 38.7%    |
| (2-slot)| 2     | 126,976      | 100,000         | 100,000        | 78.7%    |
| cheap   | 3     | 83,285       | 100,000         | 83,285         | 100%     |

The 2026-09-16 design review measured that this is **not** simply a capacity problem: prompt-eval throughput falls from ~676 tok/s at 2K context to ~37 tok/s at 100K, and a full 100K cold prefill extrapolates to 20-45 minutes of single-slot occupancy. A uniform ratio that scales the warm cap with per-slot capacity would imply ~20 tok/s prefill and hour-scale slot monopolisation on the 1-slot fast profile. The warm cap is an **economic/latency** limit driven by absolute context length, while the per-slot clamp is a **physical** capacity limit. The two must be modelled separately.

## Users

- **As a proxy operator**, I want thresholds derived from `local_model_ctx_size` and slot count so a profile change (e.g. a smaller model or a 2-slot schedule) needs no manual threshold arithmetic.
- **As a capacity planner**, I want a documented, configurable economic ceiling so the latency/utilisation trade-off is explicit and auditable.
- **As an on-call engineer**, I want startup logs to show the computed clamp, ceiling and effective thresholds per mode so a misconfiguration is visible immediately.

## Existing state

- `effective_per_slot_threshold(ctx_size, slots)` returns `ctx_size // slots - 4096` (0 when not meaningful) — `proxy/proxy/provider.py`.
- `_effective_large_context_thresholds(config)` clamps **only** warm to the per-slot cap; cold is deliberately left unclamped so the `(cold, warm]` band is non-empty for the `cached_ratio` check (LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP).
- The hard-routing caps (fast 70K / cheap 61.4K) were reverted to dynamic by LP-0MTLB1LK80098R43; the per-slot clamp + warm config are the only binding values.
- Current effective values: fast warm 100,000 (38.7% of cap), cheap warm 83,285 (100% of cap), cold 38,000 / 42,000.
- Cache warmth is bimodal (42.5% cold at 0.0-0.1, 46.1% fully warm at 0.95-1.0), so the warm cap binds almost exclusively on fully-warm requests; eviction can invalidate a warm claim.

## Desired change

Adopt a **3-term model** for the warm threshold:

1. **Physical term** — the per-slot clamp `local_model_ctx_size // slots - 4096` (unchanged, already correct).
2. **Economic term** — a latency-derived ceiling that scales with the **model** context size (not slot count): `economic_ceiling = round(local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio × local_model_ctx_size)`. The shipped ratio is `0.3815` (= 100000 / 262144), calibrated to the ~37 tok/s @100K throughput floor.
3. **Effective warm** = `min(physical_term, economic_ceiling)`.

The per-slot term dominates when `slots >= 3` (the clamp binds); the economic term dominates when `slots == 1`.

The absolute `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold`, when set, is retained as an additional upper bound (`economic_ceiling = min(ratio × ctx, warm_threshold)`) for backward compatibility; a ratio of 0 falls back to the absolute value, and both 0 disables the warm cap as today.

The **cold** threshold remains a fixed per-mode economic new-token value (fast 38,000 / cheap 42,000), is not clamped or scaled, and the `(cold, warm]` band stays non-empty.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A new economic-ceiling helper computes `round(local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio × local_model_ctx_size)`, capped by `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold` when that is > 0; returns 0 (disabled) when both inputs are 0.
- [ ] `_effective_large_context_thresholds()` resolves warm as `min(effective_per_slot_threshold(ctx_size, slots), economic_ceiling)`; with the shipped config (ratio 0.3815, ctx 262144) the computed values are fast (1 slot) = 100,000, 2-slot = 100,000, cheap (3 slots) = 83,285.
- [ ] The economic ceiling scales with model context size: with `local_model_ctx_size = 131072` and 1 slot the effective warm is ~50,000 (linear scaling test).
- [ ] The cold threshold remains a fixed per-mode value, is never clamped or scaled by per-slot capacity, and the `(cold, warm]` band is non-empty for every shipped profile (regression guard for LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP).
- [ ] Startup validation logs, for the active mode, the computed physical clamp, economic ceiling and effective warm/cold thresholds; the existing `min_local_routing_threshold` warning still fires when the physical clamp falls below the minimum.
- [ ] Unit tests assert: 1/2/3-slot scaling; ceiling scaling with model ctx; ratio=0 falls back to the absolute override; both 0 disables; band non-collapse; and that fast warm never exceeds the economic ceiling even when the per-slot clamp is larger.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (config comments in `proxy/config.yaml`, `proxy/config-fast.yaml`, `proxy/config-cheap.yaml`; `docs/llama-router.md`).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The warm threshold must **not** be raised above the latency-derived economic ceiling — measured prefill throughput makes hour-scale single-slot monopolisation unacceptable (design review, 2026-09-16).
- The cold threshold must not be scaled with per-slot capacity (preserves the `(cold, warm]` band).
- Config stays mode-overlay compatible and must not require manual per-profile recalculation when slot count or model ctx changes.
- Do not include CI/CD pipeline tests.
- CHANGELOG.md is out of scope (managed by the ship skill).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `effective_per_slot_threshold`, `_effective_large_context_thresholds`, `_get_warm_cache_threshold`; add the economic-ceiling helper and ratio reader.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — add `local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio` (0.3815) and update the warm/cold threshold comments.
- `proxy/config-fast.yaml`, `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` — document the derived values; no manual absolute recalculation.
- `proxy/proxy/compaction.py`, `proxy/proxy/router.py`, `proxy/proxy/session.py` — consumers of `effective_per_slot_threshold` (verify no behaviour regression).
- `proxy/proxy/utils.py` / startup validation path — log the computed clamp, ceiling and effective thresholds.
- `proxy/tests/` — new/updated tests for proportional scaling, ceiling scaling, band non-collapse and startup logging.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the economic-ceiling ratio `0.3815` (100000 / 262144) is the correct runtime calibration encoding the ~37 tok/s @100K throughput floor. Implementation may also expose `local_large_context_min_prefill_tps` for documentation/validation, but the ratio is the runtime source.
- **Risk (cache-warmth reliability):** warmth is bimodal and eviction can invalidate a "warm" claim; mitigation: keep the ceiling conservative and rely on the session persistence cap (`session_slot_max_prompt_tokens`).
- **Risk (band collapse):** clamping cold with warm would make the `cached_ratio` check unreachable; AC4 guards this.
- **Risk (model ctx mismatch):** `local_model_ctx_size` must match the local model's `ctx-size` in `models.ini`; startup validation should surface a mismatch.
- **Risk (scope creep):** per-request dynamic ceilings or tokenizer-accuracy changes (LP-0MSEGPO77005CYCQ) are out of scope — record as linked work instead.

## Related work

- LP-0MU1RXF6R004S8XL (completed) — documented that the threshold does not scale with per-slot capacity; decision deferred to this item.
- LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1 (completed) — introduced the per-slot clamp (physical term).
- LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S (completed, reverted) — hard-routing cap implementation; removed by LP-0MTLB1LK80098R43.
- LP-0MTLB1LK80098R43 (completed) — reverted the hard caps to dynamic derivation.
- LP-0MU5A4QBR003YJM0 (completed) — cheap mode serves economically-bypassed large contexts locally.
- LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP (completed) — collapsed-band bug the design must not reintroduce.
- Parent epic LP-0MU1S617L002Q9PR — root cause #3 (large-context routing threshold does not scale with per-slot capacity).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MQS6MPCY000A1DN** – Phase 1: Core JobScheduler - slot state tracking (completed)
- **LP-0MTQYIK4Z008XF2V** – Change the number of queued local items between fast and cheap (completed)
- **LP-0MT1F4JAK0057OJN** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/llm/.worklog/worktrees/wl-LP-0MSY0V4ZO002ANPL-set-cheap-mode-cold-threshold-to-38000-w/proxy/config-cheap.yaml:122 — Unexpected indentation (invalid-syntax) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: absolute, acceptance, actual, adding, applied (+110 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: absolute, acceptance, actual, adding, applied (+110 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: absolute, acceptance, actual, adding, applied (+110 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Design model — adopt the 3-term model (physical per-slot clamp + latency-derived economic ceiling), keep the uniform-ratio design, or a hybrid?" — Answer (operator@producer): Recommended option **A** — adopt the 3-term model. Source: interactive reply 2026-09-30 (`as recommended`).
- Q2: "How should the economic ceiling be derived?" — Answer (operator@producer): Recommended option **A** — derive from the prefill-throughput floor and scale linearly with `local_model_ctx_size` (262,144 ctx => ~100K; 131,072 ctx => ~50K). Source: interactive reply 2026-09-30.
- Q3: "Should the cold (new-token) threshold scale with per-slot capacity?" — Answer (operator@producer): Recommended option **A** — no; keep the fixed per-mode economic value (fast 38,000 / cheap 42,000) so the `(cold, warm]` band stays non-empty. Source: interactive reply 2026-09-30.
- Q4 (additional finding): "Priority — creator set `critical`; the acceptance guide lands this at `high` (major behaviour change blocking the parent epic, but not security, data loss or a broken build)." — Answer (operator@producer): accepted the recommendation — priority set to `high`. Source: interactive reply 2026-09-30.
- Citation for the design-review evidence (Q1/Q2 rationale): work-item comment by `agent` dated 2026-09-16T15:27:22Z on LP-0MU466L1X003RTHN.

# Exhaustion diagnostics: expose usage-limit quarantine and derive retry_after from it

**Parent:** LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO

## Problem

`_log_exhausted_providers` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:4106`) only inspects entry-name and
brand cooldowns, so accounts quarantined by `usage_limit_reset_pending`
(`_usage_reset_at`, `proxy/proxy/provider.py:3190`) are invisible. During the overnight
incident the exhausted payload was `unavailable={}` even though `opencode-go-3` had ~9h and
`opencode-go-2` ~13.9 days of reset remaining.

Additionally, `_providers_outside_window` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:1984`) only checks
`_is_within_allowed_window`, so a provider that is both quarantined and outside its window is
reported solely as `outside_time_window`, misattributing the cause.

## Change

- Add usage-limit quarantine to the exhaustion payload/`unavailable` map with remaining reset
  seconds and a distinct status/reason (e.g. `usage_limit_reset`).
- When recording diagnostics, prefer the true skip reason: quarantine before window.
- Ensure `_compute_retry_after` reflects the soonest real availability across cooldowns,
  windows and quarantine (it already reads `_usage_reset_at`; verify it is surfaced in the
  response).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An exhausted chain with a quarantined account includes that account (and its reset
      seconds) in `unavailable_providers`/`diagnostics` with a `usage_limit_reset` status.
- [ ] A provider that is both quarantined and outside its window is reported once, with
      `usage_limit_reset` as the reason.
- [ ] `retry_after` is > 0 and consistent with the soonest of cooldown/window/quarantine.
- [ ] Tests cover quarantine-only, quarantine+window, and quarantine+cooldown mixes.

## References

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py:4106`, `:1984`, `:3190`, `:3279`
- Related: LP-0MSLJPOCC0001ROJ (GoUsageLimitError reset), LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW (account keying)

# Intake Brief: Stream finish errors — close the recovery-first + informative-error loop

**Epic**: LP-0MUI5B98B0080CIB · Cross-repo (llm + ContextHub)

## Problem statement

The daily proxy-usage report raises a `[HIGH]` recommendation to *"adopt
recovery-first + informative-error strategy"* for stream-finish errors, but
both strategies are already implemented and shipped, and the report's own
evidence confirms every residual event carries the enriched payload — so the
recommendation tells operators to adopt something they already run. The
residual errors are instead (a) upstream `stall_after_content` (idle timeout
*after* content is delivered, where re-route is impossible), and (b)
`local/Qwen3` `RemoteProtocolError` events killed by mode-switch /
llama-server restarts that still terminate in-flight streams despite the
bounded drain. End-to-end the loop is not closed: pi-ai maps
`finish_reason: "error"` to the generic string `Provider finish_reason: error`,
discarding the enriched `type`/`message`/`suggested_action` before the client
sees it, and ContextHub's recovery extension does not match that string — so
it classifies the error as `UNKNOWN` and does **not** retry.

## Users

- **Operators/producers reading the daily proxy-usage report** — need
  recommendations that reflect the deployed state and point at the residual
  root cause rather than prescribing already-shipped strategy.
  - *As an operator, I want the stream-error recommendation to tell me which
    residual cause dominates and what (if anything) is actionable, so I don't
    chase work that was already done.*
- **Pi/agent users dispatched through ContextHub (herdr)** — whose sessions
  die with a client-visible `finish_reason: error` mid-generation.
  - *As an agent-runner user, I want a transient proxy stream error to be
    retried automatically (with the provider's suggested action surfaced), so
    a long task is not lost to an unrecoverable-looking error.*
- **Proxy maintainers** — need the restart kill-window closed or explicitly
  classified so the resident error count is attributable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **1. Adoption-aware, root-cause-classified report recommendation.** When the
   enriched stream-error payload is present, `_error_recommendations()` in the
   analysis skill no longer emits an "adopt recovery-first + informative-error"
   recommendation; it states the strategy is live and breaks the residual
   events down by root cause. Verified by unit tests over a fixture window and
   by regenerating the 2026-09-26 report.
- **2. Root-cause classification is surfaced.** Each `stream_finish_error` event
   is classified (at minimum `upstream_stall_after_content`,
   `mode_switch_restart`, `remote_chain_exhaustion`, `other`) from log fields
   and restart correlation, and the classification appears in the report, the
   taxonomy table, and `errors.csv` / `errors.json`. Verified by fixture tests
   asserting the 2026-09-26 split (24 / 6 / 1).
- **3. Client-side recovery closes the loop (ContextHub `WL` child).** The
   proxy's stream error (`Provider finish_reason: error` / `finish_reason:
   error`) is classified as retryable in ContextHub's recovery extension and
   retried with backoff, without regressing the existing nine error
   categories. Verified by a dedicated test in `error-classification.test.ts`
   (and the recovery-loop tests).
- **4. Residual restart kills fixed or explicitly classified.** An in-flight
   local stream survives a mode-switch / llama-server restart, or — if not
   feasible — the restart-kill class is deterministically classified and
   documented with rationale. Verified by regression tests covering both
   manual and scheduled switches (`test_mode_switch_drain.py`) and log
   correlation over the next transition window.
- **5. Upstream issue raised; documentation and suites green.** A tracked issue
   is raised against `@earendil-works/pi-ai` to forward the enriched
   `type`/`message`/`suggested_action` to clients (URL recorded on this item);
   all related documentation is updated in both repositories (code comments,
   `proxy/README.md`, the analysis-skill `SKILL.md`); and the full project
   test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Do not re-implement the shipped strategies.** Recovery-first re-route
  (`_preflight_streaming_response()`), the informative error builder
  (`_build_stream_error_event()`), and the bounded drain (`mode.py`) are live
  (LP-0MSETOTWY000SU0Z, LP-0MT631JKW008WAKE / LP-0MT60S55M000TK1H). Target only
  the residual gaps above.
- **Preserve LP-0MSF9RUSQ007M346's "no long rejection window" property** for
  any restart-handling change; keep llama-server `--parallel` / slot counts
  aligned with config.
- **Cross-repo tracking:** the client-side change ships in ContextHub and must
  be a child work item in the ContextHub worklog (prefix `WL`), linked back to
  this LP epic (producer decision Q3). The upstream pi-ai fix is an external
  issue, not code in either repo.
- **No new dependencies** in ContextHub for the recovery-pattern change.
- **Report change must stay data-driven** — classification from log evidence
  only; no hardcoded event counts.

## Existing state

- `[HIGH]` recommendation source: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/recommendations.py`
  (`_error_recommendations()`), firing whenever `stream_finish_error > 0` and
  always prescribing adoption regardless of enriched-payload coverage.
- Today's report (2026-09-26, window 2026-09-25 05:00 → 2026-09-26 05:00):
  31 `stream_finish_error` + 7 `stream_error` events; `errors.csv` /
  `errors.json` live in `~/proxy-usage-reports/`.
- Proxy drain: `proxy/proxy/mode.py` (`_begin_drain()`, `draining()`,
  `set_mode()`, `_spawn_restart()`); config `server.mode_switch_drain`
  (`max_seconds` 30 fast / 30 cheap, base 90).
- Log correlation: restart at 17:27:58 killed 2 local streams at 17:28:00;
  restart at 14:10:19 killed 1; scheduled 10:00 switch killed 3.
- Client: ContextHub `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/`
  (`error-patterns.ts` `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_PATTERNS`, `error-classification.ts`,
  `register-recovery.ts`); pi-ai `mapStopReason()` in
  `@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/providers/openai-completions.js` returns
  `{ stopReason: "error", errorMessage: "Provider finish_reason: error" }`.
- Prior work: LP-0MSETOTWY000SU0Z (fallback on `finish_reason:error`, shipped),
  LP-0MT60S55M000TK1H (investigation + drain + enriched logging, shipped),
  LP-0MT6322OT00900OX (enriched log line), LP-0MRDHCYNZ0092DUE (proxy hangs),
  ContextHub WL-0MR4WJRGA00536X4 (retry `Stream ended without finish_reason`).

## Desired change

1. **Analysis skill** — replace the stale `[HIGH]` recommendation with an
   adoption-aware, root-cause-classified one; add the classification to
   `errors.csv`/`errors.json` and the report's error section; update the
   skill's `SKILL.md` interpretation guidance.
2. **Proxy** — close (or deterministically classify and document) the
   mode-switch restart kill-window for in-flight local streams; add regression
   coverage.
3. **ContextHub (WL child)** — add a retryable classification for the proxy's
   `finish_reason: error` / `Provider finish_reason: error` in the recovery
   extension, with tests; surface the proxy's `suggested_action` where the
   client can access it.
4. **Upstream** — raise a pi-ai issue to forward the enriched error payload
   (`type`/`message`/`suggested_action`) so future clients can act on it
   without generic-string matching.

Decomposition into children (LLM proxy workstreams + the ContextHub `WL`
child) is performed in the plan phase.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/recommendations.py` — Replace the stale stream-finish recommendation with an adoption-aware, root-cause-classified one.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — Carry per-event root-cause classification (error_type + restart correlation) into the result model.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` — Parse restart/mode-switch markers needed to correlate `stream_finish_error` events with restarts.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — Render the classified breakdown in the error section and taxonomy.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — Fixture tests for recommendation wording and classification counts.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` — Update interpretation guidance and the root-cause taxonomy.
- `proxy/proxy/mode.py` — Ensure in-flight local streams survive the mode-switch restart, or classify restart kills deterministically.
- `proxy/proxy/router.py`, `proxy/proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/proxy/proxy_remote.py` — Stream-error construction and local/remote error paths in scope for classification.
- `proxy/tests/test_mode_switch_drain.py` — Regression tests for manual + scheduled switch behaviour.
- `proxy/config.yaml`, `proxy/config-fast.yaml`, `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` — `server.mode_switch_drain` settings if the window needs tuning.
- **ContextHub** `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts` — Add a retryable pattern for `finish_reason: error`.
- **ContextHub** `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-classification.test.ts` — Test the new classification and no-regression across categories.
- **ContextHub** `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` — Wiring if `suggested_action` is surfaced.

## Related work

- **LP-0MSETOTWY000SU0Z** – Fallback to next provider on streaming `finish_reason:error` with explicit error surfacing (completed, shipped) — the recovery-first implementation.
- **LP-0MT60S55M000TK1H** – Stream finish errors: recover-first reroute + informative error fallback (completed, shipped) — prior root-cause investigation and the mode-switch drain.
- **LP-0MT6322OT00900OX** – Log enriched stream-error payload in `Stream finished` lines (completed).
- **LP-0MRDHCYNZ0092DUE** – Investigate Pi session response hangs through proxy (completed).
- **ContextHub WL-0MR4WJRGA00536X4** – retry `Error: Stream ended without finish_reason` (completed) — precedent for the client-side retryable-pattern change.
- **`proxy/docs/error-analysis-2026-08-03.md`** — the Aug 3 error-analysis plan the taxonomy generalises from.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MRDHCYNZ0092DUE** – Investigate Pi session response hangs through proxy (completed)
- **LP-0MTLGHFD10015EJG** – [MEDIUM] `/home/rgardler/projects/llm/proxy/tests/test_slots_500_fix.py:184` — Replace aliased errors with `TimeoutError` (UP041) (completed)
- **LP-0MRHV4UYE0013F6P** – Local Qwen3 dispatch lease held 180s after stream end, blocking subsequent sessions (release-on-finish) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/README.md` — matched: client, code, error, errors, finish
- `proxy/docs/error-analysis-2026-08-03.md` — matched: address, client, code, error, errors
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — keyword-only match, not relevant

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the enriched payload is genuinely discarded before the client
  (verified by reading pi-ai `mapStopReason()` in ContextHub's installed
  dependency); if a newer pi-ai forwards it, AC3 reduces to classification on
  the forwarded fields.
- **Risk (scope creep):** this epic spans two repositories plus an upstream
  tracker. Extra opportunities (e.g. richer remote-provider cooldown handling)
  must be recorded as linked work items, not absorbed here.
- **Risk (retry storm):** retrying every `finish_reason: error` client-side
  could amplify load when the failure is terminal (e.g. all providers in
  cooldown). Mitigation: bounded exponential backoff (existing recovery
  engine) and distinguishing recoverable from terminal classes where the
  payload is available.
- **Risk (drain regression):** extending the drain must not reintroduce a long
  rejection window (LP-0MSF9RUSQ007M346); bound it and keep new-request
  deferral short with `Retry-After`.
- **Risk (classification drift):** log-format changes may drop restart markers;
  classification must degrade gracefully (fall back to `other`) and never
  fabricate counts.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Primary scope / deliverable.** Answer (producer, interactive):
  **(a)** Cross-repo epic — (i) evidence-consistent report recommendation +
  root-cause classification, (ii) client-side recovery in ContextHub,
  (iii) residual mode-switch restart kills fixed / `stall_after_content`
  documented as by-design. Source: interactive reply 2026-09-26.
- **Q2 — Client-side behaviour.** Answer (producer, interactive): **(a)** Add
  a retryable pattern for `finish_reason: error` in ContextHub's
  `error-patterns.ts` and raise a separate upstream pi-ai issue to forward the
  enriched payload. Source: interactive reply 2026-09-26.
- **Q3 — ContextHub tracking.** Answer (producer, interactive): **as
  recommended** — track the client-side change as a child in the ContextHub
  `WL` worklog and link it back to this LP item. Source: interactive reply
  2026-09-26.
- **Q (agent, context)** — *Are the recommended strategies already
  implemented?* Research: yes; `_preflight_streaming_response()`,
  `_build_stream_error_event()`, and the `mode.py` drain are live and
  committed (LP-0MSETOTWY000SU0Z, LP-0MT631JKW008WAKE); today's report confirms
  31/31 enriched payloads. Evidence: report 2026-09-26, `proxy/proxy/*.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_mode_switch_drain.py`.
- **Q (agent, context)** — *Why does the client not retry?* Research: pi-ai
  `mapStopReason()` collapses `finish_reason: "error"` to `Provider
  finish_reason: error`; ContextHub's `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_PATTERNS` do not match
  it, so classification is `UNKNOWN`. Evidence:
  `@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/providers/openai-completions.js`,
  `error-patterns.ts`.
